text.p: Bristol-Myers Squibb Co said on Thursday its Cefzil oral antibiotic was found to be safe and effective to treat middle ear infections in a study of 262 children.
Cefzil is being studied as a treatment of acute otitis media, which includes recurring middle ear infections or previous treatment failures, Bristol-Myers Squibb said.
Acute otitis media is the most commonly treated illness in children under the age of five and results in 30 million doctor visits per year in the United States, the company said.

Bristol-Myers Squibb said the study conducted from December 1994 to October 1995 confirmed that the most prevalent cause of middle ear infections was Streptococcus pneumoniae, followed by Haemophilus influenzae and Morzella catarrhalis.
The results of the study show that Cefzil achieves high clinical response rates against these organisms, the company said.

Of the Streptococcus pneumoniae organisms isolated in the children, 45 percent demonstrated resistance to penicillin, while 56 percent of Haemophilus influenzae were effectively resistant to penicillin, the company said.
Amoxicillin, which is chemically related to penicillin, traditionally has been the standard therapy for treatment of middle ear infections, the company said.

The study was presented today by Dr. Samuel McLinn, a pediatrician at Scottsdale Pediatric Center, during the First World Congress of Pediatric Infectious Diseases in Acapulco, Mexico, Bristol-Myers Squibb said.
